name: Technology and Engineering
description: A systematic blueprint for software, architecture, engineering decisions, technical systems, and innovation.

guidance: Frame the report around the system purpose, operating context, constraints, and the technical question the reader must decide.
Separate stated architecture from measured runtime behavior and distinguish design intent from implementation evidence.
Trace components, interfaces, dependencies, data movement, and failure boundaries before evaluating quality attributes.
Evaluate trade-offs against explicit quality attributes such as reliability, security, scalability, maintainability, latency, and cost only when evidenced.
Use a dependency or decision flow for structural evidence; use a chart only for measured quantities with known units and coverage.
Treat recommendations as conditional engineering options with prerequisites, risks, and verification criteria.
Call out missing benchmarks, workload assumptions, threat models, operational evidence, and version context as limitations.

sections.title: System Orientation and Technical Answer
sections.purpose: Establish what the system is intended to do, its operating context, and the direct answer to the technical objective.

blocks.title: Evidence and System Profile
instructions: Identify source coverage, system boundary, versions, environments, and material missing technical context; do not treat file statistics as system metrics.

blocks.title: Technical Executive Summary
instructions: Answer the objective using the system purpose, principal design approach, most consequential trade-off, and strongest evidence.
Distinguish documented intent from observed implementation or measured behavior.

blocks.title: Engineering Findings
instructions: Surface distinct findings about boundaries, dependencies, decisions, quality attributes, and risks; attach evidence locations where available.

sections.title: Architecture, Interfaces and Dependencies
sections.purpose: Explain how responsibilities are partitioned and how control, data, and failure propagate through the system.

blocks.title: Architecture Analysis
instructions: Analyze component responsibilities, interfaces, dependency direction, state ownership, and failure boundaries.
Do not infer deployed topology or runtime behavior from conceptual diagrams alone.

blocks.title: Critical Dependency Flow
instructions: Show one evidence-backed request, data, build, or failure path with explicit hand-offs and constraints; omit if no sequence is supported.

sections.title: Design Decisions and Quality Trade-offs
sections.purpose: Evaluate why documented choices matter and which quality attributes they improve or weaken.

blocks.title: Trade-off Analysis
instructions: For each material choice, connect the chosen mechanism to benefits, costs, constraints, and affected quality attributes.
Avoid declaring a technology universally superior without workload and operating assumptions.

blocks.title: Measured Technical Evidence

chart_slot.intent: Support one stated engineering claim with comparable measured technical evidence.

fallback.message: No comparable measured technical evidence is available.

instructions: Use only measurements with explicit units, workload or test context, and comparable populations; never chart qualitative ratings as measured performance.

sections.title: Evidence, Assurance and Operational Reality
sections.purpose: Ground technical conclusions in concrete implementation, test, operational, or source evidence.

blocks.title: Technical Evidence Trail
instructions: Connect each consequential conclusion to a specification, interface, implementation detail, test, benchmark, incident, or operational observation.

blocks.title: Engineering Options and Verification
instructions: State conditional options with prerequisites, expected trade-offs, risks, and a concrete verification signal; do not invent priorities absent from the objective.

sections.title: Technical Limitations and Open Questions
sections.purpose: State what cannot be concluded and which missing evidence could change the engineering assessment.

blocks.title: Limitations and Unknowns
instructions: Identify missing workload, scale, security, reliability, cost, version, deployment, test, and operational evidence only where it affects a conclusion.
Separate absence of evidence from evidence of absence.
